newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand runs budget gap of 3.52 bln baht in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Thailand runs budget gap of 3.52 bln baht in Feb.

text.p: Thailand ran a budget deficit of 3.52 billion baht in February which brought the total deficit from October, the start of 1996/97 fiscal year, to 50.47 billion baht, a finance ministry official said on Wednesday.
The country recorded a budget surplus of 453.1 million baht in January, but a 46.69 billion baht deficit for October-January period, the official said.

According to the official statement, the government revenue in February reached 65.02 billion baht, up 7.7 percent from the same period last year. The expenditure rose 14.1 percent on the year to 68.53 billion baht.
Since the beginning of fiscal 1996/97 (October-September) until February, the government received a revenue of 306.07 billion baht while it spent 356.49 billion baht.
The government's outstanding direct foreign debt as of February stood at 127 billion baht, the statement said.
